name: Coerrance
why: Very low entry price; private, VAT paid, Victron/solar/generator/washer/radar; room in budget for a serious modernization.
risks: ~3,710h engines; system ages/specs need verification; listing exposes phone/marketplace contact rather than email.
next_step: Contact through marketplace/phone when practical; verify rig/sails, electrical architecture, moisture and VAT/title paperwork.
notes: Best low-cost Mediterranean platform so far.

name: Ohana
why: Maestro/owner-style layout in the Caribbean; potentially comfortable liveaboard platform.
risks: Chartered from new despite owner involvement; ~3,370/3,429h engines; rig/saildrive/electrical details unresolved.
next_step: Get charter records, saildrive diaphragm/service history, rig age, electrical spec and hurricane/grounding/insurance history.
notes: Needs a discount or excellent records to rise.

name: Kajsa
why: Preferred Bahamas geography, later-model 450F, 13.5kVA Onan and 48,000-BTU Cruisair already aboard; priced for a quick sale through the Navigare/Dream fleet-exit channel.
risks: Fresh broker sheet still shows a basic charter electrical setup: no solar, no watermaker, no radar and no inverter listed; 6x140Ah service batteries; ~3,033h in the current sales PDF. Lagoon structural remediation, rig/sails, saildrives and generator hours remain unknown.
stage: Detailed broker reply + listing PDF received
next_step: Get bulkhead/compression-post documentation, phase-out/maintenance file, standing rig/sails, saildrive seals, generator hours/service and tax/title status. Compare directly with Cristal at €299k.
notes: Fresh 9/2 broker package and official Navigare page describe her as a 2018 at €339k. Some older syndications still label the listing 2017 and show older engine-hour metadata.

name: Tonina
why: Price reduced from ~$420k; inexpensive way into a Lagoon 500 if underlying refit is real.
risks: 51-ft cost penalty; mechanical/electrical/structural detail still too thin to know whether the discount is real value.
next_step: Get refit receipts, rig/sails, engines/saildrives, genset/AC status, bulkhead history and recent survey.
notes: Watch closely if broker documents major upgrades.

name: Liberty
why: Extremely cheap base; duty/tax paid, 840Ah LiFePO4 (2023), ~920W solar. Could absorb a major refit and remain below budget.
risks: Engines roughly 7,000 / 10,000h; older rig/sails and likely substantial deferred mechanical capex.
next_step: Treat as project economics: price engines, saildrives, rig/sails, moisture/structure and full survey before assigning value.
notes: Cheap enough to remain interesting despite project risk.

name: Mat Leric
why: New complete mast + standing rigging 2025, main/genoa 2024, ~2.3kW solar, genset, watermaker, Starlink, A/C/heating and washer; EU VAT paid.
risks: Above preferred budget; 48-ft TCO; AGM bank likely modernization target. Crucial unknown remains why the mast was replaced.
next_step: Broker reached the French listing side; Mat Leric is still available but seeing increased seasonal demand. Questions are with seller-side broker. Wait for technical records—especially reason for 2025 mast replacement—before any action.
notes: Still available; increased buyer interest reported. No substantive technical answers yet.

name: Azuria
why: Substantial recent equipment: new 16kW Northern Lights genset (2025), large battery bank, solar, 2023 electrical work, 2019 sails.
risks: Above budget before survey/refit; 51-ft TCO; charter history/revenue use adds wear complexity.
next_step: Only advance if seller is meaningfully flexible; validate engine hours, rig, structural history and charter wear.
